jp: 夏草や兵どもが夢の跡
romaji: natsukusa ya / tsuwamono-domo ga / yume no ato
en: Summer grasses: all that is left of the warriors' dreams.
author: Bashō
note: ok (Oku no Hosomichi). Variant: ja.wikipedia prints 夢のあと.

jp: 山路来て何やらゆかしすみれ草
romaji: yamaji kite / naniyara yukashi / sumiregusa
en: Coming along a mountain path, something strangely dear: a wild violet.
author: Bashō
note: ok (Nozarashi Kikō). Variant: Bashō DB prints 菫草.

jp: 公達に狐化けたり宵の春
romaji: kindachi ni / kitsune baketari / yoi no haru
en: A fox has turned itself into a young nobleman: an evening in spring.
author: Buson
note: ok. Wording confirmed in Shiki's essay 俳人蕪村 (Aozora), which prints 公達に狐ばけたり宵の春; 化けたり is the usual kanji rendering of the same word.

jp: 月花もなくて酒のむ独り哉
romaji: tsuki hana mo / nakute sake nomu / hitori kana
en: With neither moon nor blossoms, a man drinks sake all alone.
author: Bashō
note: ok (Arano, 1689; written on a painting of a man drinking).

jp: 野を横に馬牽むけよほととぎす
romaji: no o yoko ni / uma hikimuke yo / hototogisu
en: Turn the horse sideways across the moor: a cuckoo is calling.
author: Bashō
note: Orthography adjusted: your 馬牽きむけよ -> 馬牽むけよ, the form printed from the Soryū text (ja.wikipedia). Same reading (hikimuke yo); 馬牽きむけよ is only an okurigana-supplemented rendering that I did not find verbatim. Variants: 馬引むけよ郭公 (Wikisource 1911 ed.), 馬引き向けよ (Bashō DB).

jp: これがまあつひの栖か雪五尺
romaji: kore ga mā / tsui no sumika ka / yuki goshaku
en: So this, then, is my last dwelling place? Five feet of snow.
author: Issa
note: Orthography adjusted: your 終の栖 -> つひの栖 (Issa wrote つひ in kana; all sources checked print it so). Variant: 是がまあつひの栖か雪五尺 (ja.wikiquote, haikuguy.com Issa archive).

jp: 古池や蛙飛びこむ水の音
romaji: furuike ya / kawazu tobikomu / mizu no oto
en: An old pond: a frog jumps in, the sound of water.
author: Bashō
note: ok. Variant: 蛙飛込む (ja.wikiquote).

jp: 露の世は露の世ながらさりながら
romaji: tsuyu no yo wa / tsuyu no yo nagara / sarinagara
en: This world of dew is a world of dew, and yet, and yet.
author: Issa
note: ok (Oraga Haru, 1819). Also confirmed in the haikuguy.com Issa archive.

jp: 閑さや岩にしみ入る蝉の声
romaji: shizukasa ya / iwa ni shimiiru / semi no koe
en: Such stillness: the cicadas' cries sink into the rocks.
author: Bashō
source: https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/閑さや岩にしみ入る蝉の声
note: ok (Oku no Hosomichi). Same form in Bashō DB.

jp: 化けさうな傘かす寺の時雨かな
romaji: bakesō na / kasa kasu tera no / shigure kana
en: The temple lends me an umbrella that looks ready to turn goblin: winter rain.
author: Buson
note: Corrected kana: your 化けそうな (modern kana) -> 化けさうな (historical kana, consistent with the other poems). Source (Shiki, 俳人蕪村, Aozora) prints 化さうな傘かす寺の時雨かな; け is supplied okurigana.

jp: 盗人にとり残されし窓の月
romaji: nusubito ni / torinokosareshi / mado no tsuki
en: Left behind by the thief: the moon in the window.
author: Ryōkan
note: ok as text; printed thus by the national Ryōkan society (全国良寛会). Variant: 取り残されし. Caveat: attribution is traditional (anecdote of a thief at Gogō-an); I found no primary-source text online, and one secondary site says it was first printed as Ryōkan's only in 1914.

jp: 石山の石より白し秋の風
romaji: ishiyama no / ishi yori shiroshi / aki no kaze
en: Whiter than the stones of the stone mountain: the autumn wind.
author: Bashō
note: ok (Oku no Hosomichi, at Nata-dera). Same form on ja.wikipedia and Wikisource.

jp: この道や行く人なしに秋の暮
romaji: kono michi ya / yuku hito nashi ni / aki no kure
en: This road: no one travels along it, as the autumn evening falls.
author: Bashō
note: ok; this is the form in Sono Tayori (其便), as stated in Bashō DB. Variants: この道を行く人なしに秋の暮 (letter draft), 此道や行人なしに秋の暮 (old orthography).

jp: 初しぐれ猿も小蓑をほしげ也
romaji: hatsushigure / saru mo komino o / hoshige nari
en: First winter shower: even the monkey seems to want a little straw raincoat.
author: Bashō
note: Orthography adjusted: your 初時雨...ほしげなり -> 初しぐれ...ほしげ也, the Sarumino text as printed on ja.wikipedia (也 is read なり). Variants: 初時雨猿も小蓑を欲しげなり (Bashō DB), 初しぐれ猿も小蓑をほしげなり.

jp: 名月や池をめぐりて夜もすがら
romaji: meigetsu ya / ike o megurite / yomosugara
en: Harvest moon: I walk round and round the pond all night long.
author: Bashō
note: ok. Same form on ja.wikiquote.

jp: 硯かと拾ふやくぼき石の露
romaji: suzuri ka to / hirou ya kuboki / ishi no tsuyu
en: An inkstone? I pick it up: dew in the hollow of a stone.
author: Bashō
note: ok (1689, at Futami, recalling Saigyō; from a letter to Sanpū).

jp: むざんやな甲の下のきりぎりす
romaji: muzan ya na / kabuto no shita no / kirigirisu
en: How pitiful: beneath the helmet, a cricket chirps.
author: Bashō
note: ok (Oku no Hosomichi). Same form on ja.wikipedia and ja.wikiquote. Earlier draft: あなむざんや甲の下のきりぎりす.

jp: 物いへば唇寒し秋の風
romaji: mono ieba / kuchibiru samushi / aki no kaze
en: When I speak, my lips feel cold: the autumn wind.
author: Bashō
note: Orthography adjusted: your 物言へば -> 物いへば, as printed by Bashō DB and ja.wikiquote (original: 物いへば唇寒し穐の風). 物言へば is a common kanji rendering of the same word, not an error.

jp: 戸を叩く狸と秋を惜しみけり
romaji: to o tataku / tanuki to aki o / oshimikeri
en: With the tanuki knocking at my door, I mourned the passing of autumn.
author: Buson
note: ok. Source (Shiki, 俳人蕪村, Aozora) prints 戸を叩く狸と秋を惜みけり; し is modern okurigana.

jp: 荒海や佐渡によこたふ天の河
romaji: araumi ya / Sado ni yokotau / amanogawa
en: A rough sea: stretching out over Sado, the River of Heaven.
author: Bashō
note: ok (Oku no Hosomichi). Variants: 天河 (ja.wikiquote), 横たふ (Bashō DB).

jp: 吹き飛ばす石は浅間の野分かな
romaji: fukitobasu / ishi wa Asama no / nowaki kana
en: Stones are sent flying: the autumn gale on Mount Asama.
author: Bashō
note: ok (Sarashina Kikō). Old-orthography variant: 吹とばす石はあさまの野分哉.

jp: 五月雨をあつめて早し最上川
romaji: samidare o / atsumete hayashi / Mogamigawa
en: Gathering the early-summer rains, how swiftly it runs: the Mogami River.
author: Bashō
note: ok (Oku no Hosomichi). Variant: 集めて早し (Bashō DB).

jp: いざさらば雪見にころぶ所まで
romaji: iza saraba / yukimi ni korobu / tokoro made
en: Well then, let us go snow-viewing, until we tumble over.
author: Bashō
note: ok. Variant first line in Oi no Kobumi: いざ行かむ雪見にころぶ所まで; both are listed by Bashō DB.

jp: 名月を取ってくれろと泣く子かな
romaji: meigetsu o / totte kurero to / naku ko kana
en: "Get me that harvest moon!" cries the child.
author: Issa
note: ok (Oraga Haru, 1819). Source prints 泣く子哉; ja.wikiquote prints 名月を取てくれろとなく子かな. Earlier version (1813): あの月をとってくれろと泣子哉.

jp: 旅に病んで夢は枯野をかけ廻る
romaji: tabi ni yande / yume wa kareno o / kakemeguru
en: Fallen ill on a journey, my dreams go roaming over withered fields.
author: Bashō
note: ok (Oi Nikki; his last poem). Variant: 旅に病で (Bashō DB, original orthography, same reading).

jp: やれ打つな蝿が手をすり足をする
romaji: yare utsu na / hae ga te o suri / ashi o suru
en: Oh, don't swat it! The fly rubs its hands, rubs its feet.
author: Issa
note: ok (1821). Source prints やれ打な蝿が手をすり足をする (つ is modern okurigana); ja.wikiquote prints やれ打つな蠅が手を摺り足をする.

jp: 我と来て遊べや親のない雀
romaji: ware to kite / asobe ya oya no / nai suzume
en: Come and play with me, sparrow without parents.
author: Issa
note: ok (Oraga Haru). Earlier version (1814): 我と来てあそぶや親のない雀.

jp: 柿くへば鐘が鳴るなり法隆寺
romaji: kaki kueba / kane ga naru nari / Hōryūji
en: As I eat a persimmon, the bell tolls: Hōryū-ji.
author: Shiki
source: https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/柿くへば鐘が鳴るなり法隆寺
note: ok (1895). Variant: 柿食へば (ja.wikiquote).

jp: 桟やいのちをからむつたかづら
romaji: kakehashi ya / inochi o karamu / tsutakazura
en: The hanging bridge: ivy vines twine around it, clinging for dear life.
author: Bashō
note: Orthography adjusted: your 桟や命をからむ蔦かづら -> 桟やいのちをからむつたかづら (Sarashina Kikō text as quoted). Wording is confirmed, but printings vary a lot and I did not find your exact kanji/kana mix verbatim: Bashō DB prints 桟橋や命をからむ蔦葛 (https://www2.yamanashi-ken.ac.jp/~itoyo/basho/sarashina/sarasina.htm); the monument reads かけはしや命をからむ蔦かつら.

jp: 隅の蜘案じな煤はとらぬぞよ
romaji: sumi no kumo / anjina susu wa / toranu zo yo
en: Spider in the corner, don't worry: I won't be sweeping away the soot.
author: Issa
note: Corrected kanji: your 蜘蛛 -> 蜘 (Issa writes kumo with the single character 蜘; 1821). Single source only (Issa archive at haikuguy.com); wording matches your memory.

jp: 木枯に岩吹きとがる杉間かな
romaji: kogarashi ni / iwa fukitogaru / sugima kana
en: In the withering wind the rocks are blown sharp, there between the cedars.
author: Bashō
note: ok (Oi Nikki; 1691, at Hōrai-ji).

jp: 鶏頭の十四五本もありぬべし
romaji: keitō no / jūshigohon mo / arinubeshi
en: Cockscombs: there must be fourteen or fifteen of them.
author: Shiki
source: https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/鶏頭の十四五本もありぬべし

jp: 蛸壺やはかなき夢を夏の月
romaji: takotsubo ya / hakanaki yume o / natsu no tsuki
en: Octopus pots: fleeting dreams beneath the summer moon.
author: Bashō
note: ok (Oi no Kobumi / Sarumino). Same form on ja.wikiquote.

jp: 芭蕉野分して盥に雨を聞く夜かな
romaji: bashō nowaki shite / tarai ni ame o / kiku yo kana
en: A gale in the banana plant; a night spent listening to rain drip into a basin.
author: Bashō
note: ok (Musashiburi). The first phrase is deliberately long (8 morae). Variant: 芭蕉野分盥に雨を聞く夜かな.

jp: 世の中は地獄の上の花見かな
romaji: yo no naka wa / jigoku no ue no / hanami kana
en: In this world, we view the blossoms on the roof of hell.
author: Issa
note: ok (1812). Source and ja.wikiquote print 花見哉 (哉 = かな).

jp: 蛤のふたみにわかれ行く秋ぞ
romaji: hamaguri no / futami ni wakare / yuku aki zo
en: Like a clam torn into shell and flesh, I part for Futami as autumn goes.
author: Bashō
note: REPLACED. Your 裏を見せ表を見せて散る紅葉 (usually printed うらを見せおもてを見せて散るもみぢ) is not Ryōkan's own composition: Teishin-ni, who recorded it in Hachisu no Tsuyu, says so, and the NDL reference service (https://crd.ndl.go.jp/reference/entry/index.php?page=ref_view&id=1000041423) traces it to Tani Bokuin's 裏ちりつ表を散つ紅葉哉, which Ryōkan murmured on his deathbed. Replacement is the closing verse of Oku no Hosomichi, whose pun has two sides (futa-mi = shell and flesh / Futami the place). Source prints 蛤の ふたみにわかれ 行く秋ぞ; original 行秋ぞ.

jp: 物書て扇引さく余波哉
romaji: mono kakite / ōgi hikisaku / nagori kana
en: I write something on the fan and tear it in two: the sorrow of parting.
author: Bashō
note: Orthography adjusted: your 物書きて扇引きさく余波かな -> 物書て扇引さく余波哉, the form printed by Bashō DB and ja.wikipedia (Soryū text). Same reading (mono kakite ōgi hikisaku nagori kana; 余波 is read nagori); your version only supplies okurigana and is not a misquote. Variants: 物書いて扇引き裂く名残かな (Bashō DB index), 物かいて扇引さく名殘哉 (Wikisource 1911 ed.).
